# milume

Notebook widgets for spatial omics that stay in sync with Python.

- Install: `pip install milume`
- Documentation: https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/
- Repository: https://github.com/ckmah/milume
- Landmarks demo (molab): https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/landmarks.py

LandmarksWidget draws selections and landmarks on tissue coordinates in AnnData or
SpatialData.

---

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/concepts/data-model-coordinates.md

# Data model and coordinates

Why milume reads AnnData and SpatialData the way it does, which coordinate frame everything shares, and what crosses between Python and the widget.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/concepts/synced-state.dark.svg" alt="Diagram: Python holds AnnData and SpatialData on disk; the widget shows a 2D map and Inspect cube. Bidirectional arrows carry selections, landmarks, focus, and Inspect window fields; dashed arrows show gene columns and image chunks fetched on demand." width="880" height="400" style="width:100%;height:auto" loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/concepts/synced-state.light.svg" alt="Diagram: Python holds AnnData and SpatialData on disk; the widget shows a 2D map and Inspect cube. Bidirectional arrows carry selections, landmarks, focus, and Inspect window fields; dashed arrows show gene columns and image chunks fetched on demand." width="880" height="400" style="width:100%;height:auto" loading="lazy">
</figure>

### AnnData is the analysis object

milume draws the AnnData you already have. Cell positions come from `obsm["spatial"]` (or another key you name with `spatial_key`), labels come from `obs` columns, and expression comes from `X`. The widget holds a reference to your AnnData. It doesn't copy `obs` and it doesn't make a dense copy of `X`, so the map always shows the object your code works on.

### What milume takes from SpatialData

A SpatialData object adds images and cell shapes. When you pass one to `milume.peek`, milume picks a table: the only table, or the one whose region links a labels element. Otherwise you name it with `table=`. The table's coordinates draw the 2D map. If the object holds exactly one 3D image and is backed by a Zarr store on disk, the widget can also open the Inspect cube. The cube's cells come from a shapes element with one polygon per cell per z plane, marked by `cell_id` and `Z_um` columns. When milume can't use an element, it warns and leaves it out, so the map still opens.

### One coordinate frame

The map, selections, landmarks and the Inspect window all use the units of the table's coordinates: micrometres for Pyxa and Xenium, pixels for CosMx. milume doesn't reproject anything. The cube takes its frame from the image's transform into the shapes' coordinate system (`global` when it exists) and supports only scale plus translation, so a window position and `obsm["spatial"]` mean the same place. CosMx stores FOV-local pixels in `obsm["spatial"]`, which is why the loading guide passes `spatial_key="global"`.

milume reads the unit from reader or NGFF metadata and falls back to cell spacing when there is none. It uses the unit only to size default raster bins.

### What Python sees: synced state

Only a few named values cross between Python and the browser after the widget opens: `selections`, `landmarks`, the focused selection, and the Inspect window (`inspect_cx`, `inspect_cy`, `inspect_open`, `volume_cut`). A selection is an analysis region. You read its cells as `obs_names` with `get_obs_names`, never as row positions, so the result survives subsetting and reordering. A landmark is a durable annotation in the same coordinates, and it round-trips through a GeoDataFrame. In marimo, wrap the widget in `mo.ui.anywidget` so cells that read these values re-run when they change.

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/concepts/design-principles.md

# Design principles

The choices behind milume ("visualize, don't compute"), so you know what to expect from the widget and what stays in your own code.

### Explore spatial biology in your notebook

milume puts a tissue map in a notebook cell so you can look, select and carry what you selected back into code. These principles explain how it does that and where it stops.

### Python owns analysis, the browser owns presentation

The widget computes only what it needs to draw and to select: raster bins, neighborhoods, probe scores and color scales. It doesn't normalize, cluster or test anything, and it never writes into your AnnData. Normalization, clustering and statistics stay in your code, with scanpy, squidpy or anything else. The measure helpers (`distances`, `composition`, `enrichment` and the others) run only when you call them and return DataFrames. They write an `obs` column only when you call `write_obs`.

### Results are plain data

Everything you take out of the widget is an ordinary object: `obs_names` for a selection, a GeoDataFrame for landmarks, and a DataFrame for a measurement. Nothing depends on milume being installed to read it later, and you can hand the same regions to another tool.

### Synced state stays small

Each widget declares its synced values as named, typed fields instead of one shared blob. A value is synced only when Python reads it, sets it or computes it. Camera, colors, layer toggles and cube settings stay in the widget. Each value has one owner, so a notebook slider and a widget control never fight over it. Controls redraw on every frame while you drag and update Python once when you let go, so dependent cells run once per gesture.

### Nothing to build

The widget's browser code is compiled ahead of time and shipped in the wheel. `pip install milume` is all a notebook user needs, with no Node or frontend toolchain. Runtime dependencies are kept small for the same reason.

### Alongside other viewers

milume is for forming intuition quickly. When you need to look at a dataset in depth, use a dedicated viewer and bring the same selections and landmarks with you.

- [Measure](../reference/api/measure.md)

- [Install](../get-started/install.md)

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/concepts/rendering.md

# How rendering works

How the 2D map and the Inspect cube draw large data in a notebook: points vs raster, lazy genes, and windowed multiscale image loading under a voxel budget.

### The 2D map: one canvas

The map is a single deck.gl canvas in flat, orthographic coordinates. Cells, selections, landmarks, drafts and neighborhood overlays all draw on it, so they can't drift apart when you pan or zoom. Marker size comes from the median distance between neighboring cells. Neighborhood expansion (k-NN or radius) runs in the browser from the coordinates. It needs no neighbor graph from Python.

The 2D map doesn't draw the tissue image or cell outlines yet. Those appear in the Inspect cube.

### Points and raster

In points mode, each cell is one marker. In raster mode, the browser sorts cells into square bins and gives each bin the mean, or the category mix, of the cells within a window around its centre. In micrometre data, the defaults are 8 µm bins and a 24 µm window. Raster suits dense sections, where points overlap and hide each other. Probe compares bins by similarity. Bins and scores live only in the browser.

<figure class="ml-hero" markdown="0">
<video class="ml-loop" autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" data-src="../assets/tools/color-layers/loop-raster" data-theme="dark" poster="../../assets/tools/color-layers/loop-raster.dark.poster.webp" aria-label="The map flips from individual points to square raster bins and back." width="960" height="600"><source src="../assets/tools/color-layers/loop-raster.dark.webm" type="video/webm"><source src="../assets/tools/color-layers/loop-raster.dark.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>
<img class="ml-loop-poster" src="../assets/tools/color-layers/loop-raster.dark.poster.webp" alt="The map flips from individual points to square raster bins and back." width="960" height="600" loading="lazy">
</figure>

### Genes load when you color by them

At startup only gene names reach the browser. A gene's column is fetched from the kernel the first time you color by it, then kept in a size-limited browser cache that never drops a gene on screen. So a whole-transcriptome panel opens as fast as a small one. `genes=[...]` preloads a short list instead, up to 64 MiB. For color, each gene is scaled from its minimum to its 99th percentile. That scaling is for display only and doesn't change `X`.

### The Inspect cube reads one window

Inspect places a 300 µm square on the map and opens a cube of that window through the full depth of the image. The browser reads only that box from one level of the image pyramid over the widget's own connection, and never reads tables or expression that way. Cells in the window are built into meshes in a Web Worker and colored from the category panel. The cube's Points layer (cell centres) is off by default.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/tools/inspect-3d/still-pill.dark.png" alt="The Inspect cube open: the top pill shows Exit, Inspect with the window size in µm, Save window, and full screen; the bottom toolbar has camera presets and layer toggles." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/tools/inspect-3d/still-pill.light.png" alt="The Inspect cube open: the top pill shows Exit, Inspect with the window size in µm, Save window, and full screen; the bottom toolbar has camera presets and layer toggles." loading="lazy">
</figure>

### Choosing an image level: the voxel budget

The hover preview uses a coarse level. The open cube picks the sharpest level whose window fits 64 Mi voxels (about 64 MB of 8-bit texture) and at most 2,048 voxels per axis. Nothing is hard-coded per dataset. On the 3D demo tier, a full-resolution window is over the budget, so the cube loads the next level.

### Which data sizes this covers

Demo data runs from tiny test fixtures to a 2D section, a 3D tier and a full colon run. Tier paths, on-disk sizes, and citations are on [Datasets](../reference/datasets.md).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/get-started/install.md

# Install

## pip

```bash
pip install milume
```

Requires Python 3.11+.

Each demo notebook lists its own dependencies in its inline script header, so
`uvx marimo edit --sandbox demos/landmarks.py` (or opening it on molab) installs
them for you. The [Squidpy recipe](../how-to/recipes/) also needs
scanpy, squidpy and leidenalg:

```bash
pip install squidpy scanpy leidenalg
```

## uv

```bash
uv pip install --compile-bytecode milume
```

`--compile-bytecode` compiles `.pyc` files at install time, so the first
`import milume` doesn't pay for compiling milume and its dependencies. In a
project, `uv add milume` works too (set `UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1` for the same
effect).

## From source

```bash
uv sync --group demo --group dev
```

The `demo` dependency group adds marimo and the spatial-omics packages used by
`demos/`. It is a development group, not a published extra.

## Next

- [Tutorial: explore cells in 2D](tutorial-explore-cells-2d.md)
- [Use with AI agents](../how-to/use-with-ai-agents.md)
- [LandmarksWidget API](../reference/api/landmarks/)
- [Open Landmarks demo](https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/landmarks.py)
- [Changelog](../reference/changelog.md): what changed in each release

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/get-started/tutorial-explore-cells-2d.md

# Tutorial: explore cells in 2D

Walk through the [ileum molab notebook](https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/ileum_2d.py) on Xu et al. 2026 ileum MERFISH ([#343](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/343)). Each step below matches one section of the notebook and shows a visible result on the map or in a table.

## 1. Load the ileum slice

Download the slice with ``ml.datasets`` or the short alias ``ml.ds`` (pinned URL, user cache). The matrix ``X`` is already the authors' log-normalized values — do not call ``normalize_total`` or ``log1p``.

```python
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
```

**Result:** `adata` is 30,332 cells × 1,815 genes with `obsm["spatial"]` in micrometres. The notebook preloads a small curated gene list in `ml.peek(..., genes=...)` so the widget export stays within the static payload budget. See the [Datasets](../reference/datasets.md#2d) reference for fields and citation.

## 2. Open the map on cell types

```python
DEMO_GENES = [
    "Apob", "Slc5a1", "Nos2", "Cps1", "Mki67", "Lgr5", "Erbb3", "H2-Eb1",
    "Acta2", "Col1a1", "Phox2b", "Kit", "Pecam1", "Mzb1", "Cd3e", "Csf1r",
    "Cxcl13", "Cr2", "Ccr7",
]
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type", genes=DEMO_GENES)
w
```

**Result:** The full ileum ring appears, coloured by `cell_type`.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/tutorials/explore-cells-2d/still-cell-types.dark.png" alt="The ileum section coloured by cell type in the Landmarks map." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/tutorials/explore-cells-2d/still-cell-types.light.png" alt="The ileum section coloured by cell type in the Landmarks map." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## 3. Layer and villus–crypt genes

Recolour in place — no new figure objects:

```python
w.color = "anatomical_layer"  # mucosa, submucosa, muscle, GALT
w.color = "Apob"              # villus-tip enterocytes
w.color = "Cps1"              # crypt / lower villus
```

**Result:** You see the crypt–villus axis and the GALT patches in anatomical layers before you select them.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/tutorials/explore-cells-2d/still-anatomical-layer.dark.png" alt="The same section coloured by anatomical layer, with GALT patches visible." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/tutorials/explore-cells-2d/still-anatomical-layer.light.png" alt="The same section coloured by anatomical layer, with GALT patches visible." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## 4. Lasso GALT cryptopatch aggregates

Use the Select tool and lasso each GALT cryptopatch on the map ([Select regions](../reference/ui/select-regions.md)). Xu et al. annotate these as small ILF-like aggregates (rich in cDC, ILC3, and FRC), not classical B/T follicles. Each edit updates `w.selections`.

The notebook seeds two tight polygons (`galt-aggregates-west` and `galt-aggregates-east`). Join them for downstream analysis:

```python
galt_hits = w.get_obs_names("galt-aggregates-west").union(
    w.get_obs_names("galt-aggregates-east")
)
```

**Result:** The seeded headless lassos select **278 cells** in total, **261** with `anatomical_layer` GALT (**93.9%** of the selection), covering **all 260** annotated GALT cells in the two cryptopatch aggregates on this slice. The western polygon is **90.2%** GALT (164 cells, 148 GALT); the tightened eastern polygon is **99.1%** GALT (114 cells, 113 GALT). Your own lassos may differ.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/tutorials/explore-cells-2d/still-galt-selection.dark.png" alt="Two GALT cryptopatch lassos on the ileum map with cell-type counts for the selection." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/tutorials/explore-cells-2d/still-galt-selection.light.png" alt="Two GALT cryptopatch lassos on the ileum map with cell-type counts for the selection." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## 5. Enrichment and violin plots

```python
enrich = ml.enrichment(adata, galt_hits, obs_key="cell_type")
enrich
```

**Result:** Stromal and innate immune types rank highest by `log2_enrichment` relative to the whole section (seeded union: FRC 6.20, cDC (Il22ra2+) 6.04, ILC3 5.66, FDC 5.35, B (follicular) 4.52).

Flag the selection and plot immune markers:

```python
adata.obs["galt_vs_rest"] = "rest"
adata.obs.loc[galt_hits, "galt_vs_rest"] = "GALT selection"
sc.pl.violin(adata, ["Mzb1", "Cd3e"], groupby="galt_vs_rest")
```

**Result:** `Mzb1` and `Cd3e` are higher in the GALT selection than in the rest of the section.

- [Datasets](../reference/datasets.md)

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/get-started/tutorial-spatialdata-3d.md

# Tutorial: 3D with SpatialData

Follow the [Landmarks molab demo](https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/landmarks.py): Pyxa `small/` from Hugging Face, clustering for colour, then **image + cell outlines → Inspect cube** ([#339](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/339), [#343](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/343)).

## 1. Load the 3D tier

Download `Stellaromics/demo` `small/` (transcript CSV omitted in the demo — about 247 MB) and build SpatialData with the Pyxa reader:

```python
from pathlib import Path

from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from spatialdata_io.experimental import pyxa

data_dir = (
    Path(
        snapshot_download(
            "Stellaromics/demo",
            repo_type="dataset",
            allow_patterns="small/*",
            ignore_patterns="*cell_assigned_gene*",
        )
    )
    / "small"
)
pyxa_sdata = pyxa(data_dir, cell_assigned_gene=False)
```

**Result:** Table with 4,372 cells, DAPI mosaic, and per-z cell outline polygons in micrometres. Details: [Datasets](../reference/datasets.md#3d).

## 2. Clusters for colour

```python
import scanpy as sc

adata = pyxa_sdata.tables["rna"]
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
sc.pp.pca(adata)
sc.pp.neighbors(adata)
sc.tl.leiden(adata, key_added="cluster", flavor="leidenalg", n_iterations=2)
pyxa_sdata.tables["rna"] = adata
```

**Result:** A `cluster` column for `milume.peek(..., color="cluster")`. The demo uses log1p on counts only — not `normalize_total`.

## 3. Write Zarr and open the map

Inspect reads the image from a SpatialData Zarr store on disk:

```python
import spatialdata as sd
import tempfile

store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="milume-")) / "small.sdata.zarr"
pyxa_sdata.write(store, overwrite=True)
sdata = sd.read_zarr(store)

import milume

w = milume.peek(sdata, color="cluster")
w
```

**Result:** Coloured cells on the 2D map over the Pyxa section.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/tutorials/spatialdata-3d/still-map-clusters.dark.png" alt="Pyxa small section on the map, coloured by Leiden cluster." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/tutorials/spatialdata-3d/still-map-clusters.light.png" alt="Pyxa small section on the map, coloured by Leiden cluster." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## 4. Inspect: image and cell meshes

Click an empty area of the widget so it has keyboard focus, then press <kbd>I</kbd> and click the tissue ([Inspect in 3D](../reference/ui/inspect-3d.md)). The DAPI cube opens with **cell outline meshes**, not points.

Use the cross-section sliders in the Inspect toolbar to move the cut plane. Saved inspect selections appear in the Selections list like lasso regions.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../assets/tutorials/spatialdata-3d/still-inspect-cube.dark.png" alt="Inspect cube on Pyxa small: DAPI image and cell outline meshes with the Points layer off." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../assets/tutorials/spatialdata-3d/still-inspect-cube.light.png" alt="Inspect cube on Pyxa small: DAPI image and cell outline meshes with the Points layer off." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## 5. Enrichment on an Inspect selection

After you save an Inspect window, read its cells and run composition:

```python
inspect_id = w.selections[-1]["id"]
hits = w.get_obs_names(inspect_id)
milume.enrichment(adata, hits, obs_key="cluster")
```

**Result:** A table of cluster proportions inside the cube window versus the whole dataset.

## 6. Drive Inspect from Python

Open or move the cube without a click when the widget already has a 3D volume:

```python
w.inspect_cx, w.inspect_cy = 120.0, 140.0
w.inspect_open = True
w.volume_cut  # read cut state after slider moves
```

Setting `inspect_open = False` closes the cube and exits Inspect. See [synced traitlets](../reference/api/landmarks.md#synced-traitlets).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/how-to/draw-export-landmarks.md

# Draw and export landmarks

Draw landmarks on the map, export them as vector data, and load edits back into the widget.

## Goal

Move landmarks between milume and GeoPandas (or any tool that reads GeoJSON/Shapefile via GeoDataFrame).

## Steps

1. Open milume on spatial data (ileum demo):

```python
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w
```

2. Draw or edit landmarks in the browser ([Landmarks](../reference/ui/landmarks.md)). Each edit updates `w.landmarks`.

3. Convert the synced list to a GeoDataFrame (`geopandas` required):

```python
import geopandas as gpd
from milume import landmarks_to_geodataframe, geodataframe_to_landmarks

gdf = landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
gdf.to_file("landmarks.geojson", driver="GeoJSON")
```

4. Edit `gdf` offline, then push it back:

```python
gdf = gpd.read_file("landmarks.geojson")
w.landmarks = geodataframe_to_landmarks(gdf)
```

5. Run measure helpers against the same `adata` and exported geometry when you need distances or composition ([Measure API](../reference/api/measure.md)).

## Result

`landmarks.geojson` (or your chosen path) matches what you drew; assigning back to `w.landmarks` updates the map.

Column semantics and CRS notes are in [GeoDataFrame interchange](../reference/api/landmarks.md#geodataframe-interchange).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/how-to/load-anndata-spatialdata.md

# Load AnnData / SpatialData

Open milume on AnnData or SpatialData you already have in the notebook.

## Goal

Show spatial cells (and, for SpatialData, the Inspect cube when a 3D image is available) with `milume.peek`.

## AnnData

1. Load AnnData with coordinates in `obsm["spatial"]` (for example the ileum demo slice):

```python
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w
```

2. If your matrix uses another `obsm` key, pass `spatial_key=` when you call `peek`.

**Result:** The Landmarks map opens on the ileum section, colored by `cell_type`.

Constructor options (`color`, `genes`, `spatial_key`, …) are in the [LandmarksWidget API](../reference/api/landmarks.md#constructor-parameters).

## SpatialData

Install the platform reader once:

```bash
pip install spatialdata-io
```

Then read with the loader for your platform and pass the object to `peek`. milume infers the table, cell polygons, and 3D image when they are present. Override with `table=`, `image=`, `labels=`, or `shapes=` when needed ([constructor parameters](../reference/api/landmarks.md#constructor-parameters)).

### Pyxa

1. Install a `spatialdata-io` build that includes the Pyxa reader (see the [Landmarks molab demo](https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/landmarks.py) pin if the release you use does not yet ship `pyxa`).

2. Read Stellaromics Pyxa output into SpatialData:

```python
from pathlib import Path

import spatialdata as sd
from spatialdata_io.experimental import pyxa

data_dir = Path("/path/to/pyxa/small")  # counts, metadata, DAPI mosaic
sdata = pyxa(data_dir, cell_assigned_gene=False)
```

3. To use **Inspect** on the DAPI mosaic, write the store to disk and reopen it (the cube reads the image from Zarr):

```python
store = Path("/tmp/pyxa.sdata.zarr")
sdata.write(store, overwrite=True)
sdata = sd.read_zarr(store)
```

4. Open milume on the table you want to color (for example `rna` after you add a cluster column):

```python
w = milume.peek(sdata, color="cluster")
w
```

**Result:** Pyxa cells and mosaic load; Inspect is available after the Zarr round-trip.

### Xenium

1. Point `spatialdata_io.xenium` at the Xenium `*_outs` folder (or a subset of its files):

```python
import spatialdata_io as sio
import milume

sdata = sio.xenium("/path/to/xenium_outs", transcripts=False)
w = milume.peek(sdata)
w
```

2. Set `w.color` to any categorical column on the table, or pass `color=` to `peek` when you open it.

**Result:** Xenium cells render in global coordinates from `obsm["spatial"]` (default `spatial_key`).

Platform-specific reader flags stay in the [spatialdata-io](https://github.com/scverse/spatialdata-io) docs.

### CosMx

1. Read CosMx flat files with `spatialdata_io.cosmx`:

```python
import spatialdata_io as sio
import milume

sdata = sio.cosmx("/path/to/cosmx_flat_files", dataset_id="my_run", transcripts=False)
```

2. Pass `spatial_key="global"`. CosMx FOV-local pixels live in `obsm["spatial"]`; milume needs global coordinates:

```python
w = milume.peek(sdata, spatial_key="global")
w
```

**Result:** CosMx cells from every FOV share one map in global pixel space.

For Inspect behavior on platforms without per-slice cell meshes, see [Inspect in 3D](../reference/ui/inspect-3d.md).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/how-to/match-plot-colors-squidpy.md

# Match plot colors (squidpy)

Color the Landmarks map from Squidpy niche labels and reuse the same hex colors in Matplotlib or Scanpy plots.

## Goal

Run Squidpy neighborhood niches on a selection, assign `w.color` to the niche column Squidpy writes, and read colors back with `w.category_colors`.

## Steps

1. Install optional analysis packages:

```bash
pip install scanpy squidpy leidenalg
```

2. Open the ileum slice and draw a region to analyze (or use the whole tissue):

```python
import milume as ml
import squidpy as sq

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w  # draw a selection in the browser, then continue
```

3. Build a boolean mask aligned to `adata.obs_names` for the selection you want:

```python
region = w.selections[-1]["id"]
mask = adata.obs_names.isin(w.get_obs_names(region))
```

4. Run Squidpy niches on that mask (neighbors + spatial graph first):

```python
sc.pp.neighbors(adata)
sq.gr.spatial_neighbors_knn(adata, n_neighs=6)
sq.gr.calculate_niche(
    adata,
    flavor="neighborhood",
    groups="cell_type",
    n_neighbors=6,
    resolutions=0.5,
    mask=mask,
)
niche_col = "nhood_niche_res=0.5"
```

5. Colour the map from the new column:

```python
w.color = niche_col
```

6. Reuse the map palette elsewhere:

```python
palette = w.category_colors(niche_col)  # {label: "#rrggbb"}
```

## Result

Landmarks points and downstream plots share the same label-to-color mapping as the map.

For a prepared studio walkthrough (fixed selection and export state), use the [Squidpy niche color recipe](recipes/squidpy_color/) or the live [molab notebook](https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/recipes/squidpy_color.py). The recipe export pipeline is unchanged; this page is the task-only steps.

Squidpy and Scanpy parameters stay in their own docs; milume traitlets are in the [LandmarksWidget API](../reference/api/landmarks.md).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/how-to/recipes/index.md

# Recipes

Each recipe is one [marimo](https://marimo.io) notebook under `demos/recipes/`. The docs site serves a **prepared** studio export (fixed widget state). Draw new selections or re-run analysis in **molab**.

Needs the same optional packages as the demos (`squidpy`, `scanpy`, `leidenalg` where noted). 2D recipes use the **ileum** tier via ``milume.datasets.ileum_merfish_xu2026()`` ([#380](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/380)).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/how-to/use-selections-downstream.md

# Use selections downstream

Carry lasso, rectangle, and inspect selections into pandas, Scanpy, or other Python analysis.

## Goal

Turn the cells inside a map selection into an observation subset or a boolean column on `adata.obs`.

## Steps

1. Open milume on AnnData with spatial coordinates (ileum demo):

```python
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w
```

2. Draw a selection in the browser ([Select regions](../reference/ui/select-regions.md)). Each edit updates `w.selections`.

3. Read the latest selection id and the cell names it covers:

```python
sel_id = w.selections[-1]["id"]
hits = w.get_obs_names(sel_id)  # pd.Index of obs_names
```

4. Join to observations by name (not row index):

```python
adata.obs["in_selection"] = adata.obs_names.isin(hits)
adata_sel = adata[hits].copy()
```

5. Run downstream code on the subset or the flag. Example summary table:

```python
import pandas as pd

summary = pd.DataFrame(
    {"cell_type": adata.obs.loc[hits, "cell_type"].value_counts()}
)
```

Use `w.get_obs_names("focus")` when the focused selection in the UI is the one you want ([Methods](../reference/api/landmarks.md#methods)).

## Result

`hits` and `adata_sel` (or `adata.obs["in_selection"]`) stay aligned with the map. Re-run steps 3–5 after you change selections in the widget.

Landmarks (`w.landmarks`) are durable geometry; selections are analysis regions. Traitlets and edge cases are in the [LandmarksWidget API](../reference/api/landmarks.md).

# Use with AI agents

Install the [use-milume](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/blob/main/skills/use-milume/SKILL.md) skill so your agent knows LandmarksWidget workflows and the public API:

```bash
npx skills add ckmah/milume --skill use-milume
```

In Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add ckmah/milume
/plugin install use-milume@milume
```

After `pip install milume`, copy the skill that matches your installed version (stdlib only, no Node):

```bash
python -m milume.skill install
```

Optional target directory and overwrite:

```bash
python -m milume.skill install ./.agents/skills --force
```

# milume

Layer images, cells, and transcripts in 3D, in one reactive widget.

```python
import milume

w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
```

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/api/datasets.md

# Datasets

Load milume demo AnnData from pip or molab without a git checkout ([#380](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/380)).

```python
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
names = ml.datasets.list_datasets()
meta = ml.datasets.info("ileum_merfish_xu2026")
path = ml.datasets.fetch("ileum_merfish_xu2026")
```

``ml.ds`` is an alias for the same module object as ``ml.datasets`` (``ml.ds is ml.datasets``). Use either name after ``import milume as ml``.

Downloads use stdlib ``urllib``, stream to a ``.part`` file, verify a pinned sha256, then rename into place. The cache root is ``$MILUME_DATA_DIR``, then ``$XDG_CACHE_HOME/milume``, then ``~/.cache/milume``. URLs are pinned to an immutable git ref (never ``main``).

## ileum_merfish_xu2026

`ileum_merfish_xu2026(*, path=None, force_download=False, **read_kwargs) -> anndata.AnnData`

Xu et al. 2026 MERFISH mouse ileum (one SPF cross-section). Shape **30,332 × 1,815**. ``X`` is log-normalized; do not re-normalize.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Size | 5,014,135 B |
| sha256 | `059ebea8360dc95e008a06dde26fac8f1a6f76f323d92151b1bfc305df5786a1` |
| License | CC0-1.0 ([Dryad](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.p5hqbzm0z)) |
| Citation | Xu RJ, et al. *Cell Host & Microbe* 34(3):509–525.e13 (2026); Dryad doi:10.5061/dryad.p5hqbzm0z |

## list_datasets

`list_datasets() -> list[str]`

Registered dataset names (v1: ``ileum_merfish_xu2026`` only).

## info

`info(name) -> DatasetInfo`

Registry metadata: ``name``, ``kind``, ``size_bytes``, ``n_obs``, ``n_vars``, ``license``, ``citation``, ``url``, ``sha256``.

## fetch

`fetch(name, *, path=None, force_download=False) -> pathlib.Path`

Return a local path, downloading when needed. ``force_download=True`` replaces a valid cache entry.

## DatasetInfo

Frozen dataclass with the same fields as ``info()``.

## Tier reference

Other demo tiers (tiny fixtures, Pyxa ``xsmall``/``small``, colon) stay on checkout paths or Hugging Face until later registry entries ([#343](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/343)).

See also the [Datasets tier table](datasets.md) for fields, citations, and in-repo paths.

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/api/landmarks.md

# LandmarksWidget API

Generated from `milume` sources. For narrative guides, see [Tutorial: explore cells in 2D](../../get-started/tutorial-explore-cells-2d.md).

## `peek()`

```python
def peek(data, **kwargs) -> LandmarksWidget
```

Open a Milume surface on AnnData or SpatialData.

Main notebook entry point for interactive landmarks. Constructs
`LandmarksWidget` with the same keyword arguments.

#### Parameters

- **data, adata** — AnnData with spatial coordinates, or SpatialData (volume inferred). `milume.peek` names this argument `data`; `LandmarksWidget` names the same argument `adata`.
- **spatial_key** — `obsm` key for x/y coordinates (default `"spatial"`).
- **color** — `obs` column or `var_names` gene for point colour. When omitted, the first detected categorical column is used. Assign `w.color = key` later to recolour; unknown keys raise before anything changes.
- **genes** — Genes offered for view-only colouring. `None` (default) offers every `var_name` and sends each gene's values only when it is first coloured. A name or list restricts the catalog and preloads it when it packs under 64 MiB; larger lists load on demand too, with a warning.
- **table, image, shapes** — SpatialData-only overrides for the inferred table, multiscale image, and the shapes element of per-slice cell polygons (`cell_id` and `Z_um` columns) the Inspect cube meshes. `False` leaves one out.
- **channels** — SpatialData-only channel names to show on open (e.g. `["DAPI"]`). Unknown names raise `ValueError` listing the available names. For 3D images only one channel is allowed in this version.
- **contrast_limits** — SpatialData-only image contrast `(min, max)` for the Inspect cube. Defaults to the coarsest pyramid level's 1st percentile and max.

#### Notes

The widget keeps a reference to `adata` (no `obs.copy()`, no full-`X`
densify at construct). Chrome follows the notebook cell width; height starts
at 720px and is resizable. `point_size` is the marker radius in the same
units as `obsm` x/y (not a visibility flag). It is seeded at 0.4 times the
median nearest-neighbor distance. `_cells_visible` hides the dots and
restores that same radius. When a micrometre scale is known (`_um_per_unit`,
from a SpatialData coordinate system in micrometres, an AnnData
`uns['spatial']` scale factor, or `uns['spatial_units']`), the Layers
slider edits dot diameter from 1 to 50 µm and the seeded radius is clamped
into that range. With no scale, `point_size` stays in raw coordinate units
and the slider labels them px. Neighbourhood expand runs in the browser from
coordinates; no `obsp` graphs are required.

UI chrome (mode, neighbourhoods, raster controls) stays in the browser and
is not part of the notebook API. Raster bins and probe scores are built
client-side from the loaded gene, embedding, and category packs.

#### Returns

- **LandmarksWidget** — Widget handle `w`. Synced traitlets include `w.selections` and `w.landmarks`; join to `adata` with `get_obs_names(region)`.

#### Examples

```python
import milume
w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w = milume.peek(sdata)  # table, image, cell polygons inferred
```

---

## Constructor parameters

#### Parameters

- **data, adata** — AnnData with spatial coordinates, or SpatialData (volume inferred). `milume.peek` names this argument `data`; `LandmarksWidget` names the same argument `adata`.
- **spatial_key** — `obsm` key for x/y coordinates (default `"spatial"`).
- **color** — `obs` column or `var_names` gene for point colour. When omitted, the first detected categorical column is used. Assign `w.color = key` later to recolour; unknown keys raise before anything changes.
- **genes** — Genes offered for view-only colouring. `None` (default) offers every `var_name` and sends each gene's values only when it is first coloured. A name or list restricts the catalog and preloads it when it packs under 64 MiB; larger lists load on demand too, with a warning.
- **table, image, shapes** — SpatialData-only overrides for the inferred table, multiscale image, and the shapes element of per-slice cell polygons (`cell_id` and `Z_um` columns) the Inspect cube meshes. `False` leaves one out.
- **channels** — SpatialData-only channel names to show on open (e.g. `["DAPI"]`). Unknown names raise `ValueError` listing the available names. For 3D images only one channel is allowed in this version.
- **contrast_limits** — SpatialData-only image contrast `(min, max)` for the Inspect cube. Defaults to the coarsest pyramid level's 1st percentile and max.

#### Notes

The widget keeps a reference to `adata` (no `obs.copy()`, no full-`X`
densify at construct). Chrome follows the notebook cell width; height starts
at 720px and is resizable. `point_size` is the marker radius in the same
units as `obsm` x/y (not a visibility flag). It is seeded at 0.4 times the
median nearest-neighbor distance. `_cells_visible` hides the dots and
restores that same radius. When a micrometre scale is known (`_um_per_unit`,
from a SpatialData coordinate system in micrometres, an AnnData
`uns['spatial']` scale factor, or `uns['spatial_units']`), the Layers
slider edits dot diameter from 1 to 50 µm and the seeded radius is clamped
into that range. With no scale, `point_size` stays in raw coordinate units
and the slider labels them px. Neighbourhood expand runs in the browser from
coordinates; no `obsp` graphs are required.

UI chrome (mode, neighbourhoods, raster controls) stays in the browser and
is not part of the notebook API. Raster bins and probe scores are built
client-side from the loaded gene, embedding, and category packs.

## Synced traitlets

Public traitlets from the registry (`milume.landmarks._PUBLIC_TRAITS`). Other synced fields are internal plumbing and may change without notice.

<div class="milume-api-traitlet-table" markdown="1">

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | str | list[str] | `""` | obs column, gene, gene list (blend), or obsm embedding key; assign to recolour (raises ColorKeyError / ColorValueError). |
| `selections` | List[Dict] | `[]` | Drawn selections as dicts with id, name, geometry and point indices. |
| `landmarks` | List[Dict] | `[]` | Drawn landmarks (points, lines, splines, shapes) as dicts. |
| `selected_kind` | str | `""` | Kind of the focused item: selection, landmark, type, or empty. |
| `selected_index` | int | `-1` | Index of the focused item within its kind, or -1. |
| `selected_type_indices` | List[Int] | `[]` | Focused category label indices when selected_kind is type. |
| `inspect_cx` | float | `None` | Inspect window centre x in spatial units, or None before placement; set it to move the window and the open cube. |
| `inspect_cy` | float | `None` | Inspect window centre y in spatial units, or None before placement; set it to move the window and the open cube. |
| `inspect_size_um` | float | `300.0` | Inspect window side length in µm. |
| `inspect_open` | bool | `False` | Whether the Inspect cube is open; True opens it at inspect_cx/cy, or at the volume centre when no window is placed; False closes it and exits Inspect. ValueError without a 3D image. |
| `volume` | dict | — | The 3D image behind the Inspect cube (image path, cell polygons path and size, voxel size, origin, contrast); {} without one. Read it, don't set it. |
| `volume_cut` | List[Float] | `[]` | Cube cut box [x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1] in µm; the browser writes it on slider release, assign it to cut from Python. |
| `active_category` | str | `""` | Deprecated: derived from color; removed in 3.0. |
| `active_genes` | List[Unicode] | `[]` | Deprecated: derived from color; removed in 3.0. |

</div>

## GeoDataFrame interchange

Convert `w.landmarks` to a durable GeoPandas table (and back). Control vertices live in a JSON `vertices` column; `geometry` is a GIS proxy. The widget does not own SpatialData — assign `sdata['landmarks'] = gdf` in the notebook if needed.

Requires optional `geopandas` and `shapely`.

### `landmarks_to_geodataframe()`

```python
def landmarks_to_geodataframe(landmarks: list[dict] | None)
```

Convert widget landmark dicts to a GeoDataFrame.

#### Parameters

- **landmarks** — Landmark dicts from `w.landmarks`, or `None` / `[]` for an empty frame with contract columns (`id`, `type`, `vertices`, …).

#### Returns

- **geopandas.GeoDataFrame** — Proxy `geometry` plus JSON `vertices` as the round-trip source of truth. Callers assign into SpatialData themselves (e.g. `sdata["landmarks"] = gdf`).

#### Examples

```python
import milume
w = milume.peek(adata)
gdf = milume.landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
len(gdf)
```
0

### `geodataframe_to_landmarks()`

```python
def geodataframe_to_landmarks(gdf)
```

Convert a landmarks GeoDataFrame back to widget dicts.

#### Parameters

- **gdf** — GeoDataFrame produced by `landmarks_to_geodataframe`, or `None` / zero rows.

#### Returns

- **list[dict]** — Widget landmark dicts suitable for `w.landmarks = ...`. Empty input yields `[]`.

#### Examples

```python
import milume
w = milume.peek(adata)
w.landmarks = milume.geodataframe_to_landmarks(
```
...     milume.landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
... )

## Methods

Notebook helpers on the widget handle returned by `milume.peek`.

### `category_colors()`

```python
def category_colors(column: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]
```

Label -> hex colour of a categorical column, as the map draws it.

Defaults to the active category. Use it to colour other views (plots,
the cube) the same way as the points.

### `clear_selections()`

```python
def clear_selections() -> None
```

Remove every selection from the widget.

### `clear_landmarks()`

```python
def clear_landmarks() -> None
```

Remove every landmark from the widget.

### `clear()`

```python
def clear() -> None
```

Remove all selections and landmarks.

### `select_type()`

```python
def select_type(index: int) -> None
```

Focus one category group in the active set (replaces a multi-select union).

The browser may set `selected_type_indices` to several groups; this
helper is the notebook path for single-group focus without fighting
front-end sync.

### `get_obs_names()`

```python
def get_obs_names(region: str) -> 'pd.Index'
```

`obs_names` of the cells in `region` as a `pd.Index`.

`region` is a selection id from `w.selections`, or `"focus"` for
the focused selection or category groups (empty when nothing is
focused). A hidden selection still returns its cells; hiding only
affects display. Raises `KeyError` for an unknown id. Write a column with
`adata.obs[key] = adata.obs_names.isin(w.get_obs_names(region))`.

### `set_points()`

```python
def set_points(x: Any, y: Any) -> None
```

Move the scatter points; colour stays on `color`.

### `set_expression()`

```python
def set_expression(expr: Any) -> None
```

Replace the gene catalog from a table (view-only).

Every column becomes a gene; it preloads under the eager size limit and
loads on demand above it, like `genes=`.

### `set_render_mode()`

```python
def set_render_mode(mode: str) -> None
```

Switch canvas between point scatter and spatial raster bins.

### `set_raster_basis()`

```python
def set_raster_basis(*, genes: str | None = None, embedding: str | None = None, composition: str | None = None) -> None
```

Select bin aggregation basis (genes / embedding / composition).

Bin feature matrices are built in the browser; this only updates traits.

### `clear_raster_query()`

```python
def clear_raster_query() -> None
```

Clear the pinned similarity query bin.

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/api/measure.md

# Measure

Quantify landmarks and selections in Python. Every function returns a tidy `pandas.DataFrame` with one row per cell (or per group).

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/measure/hero.dark.png" alt="Left: the widget with one spline landmark and a wide buffer. Right: a histogram of each cell's distance to that landmark." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/measure/hero.light.png" alt="Left: the widget with one spline landmark and a wide buffer. Right: a histogram of each cell's distance to that landmark." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## Setup

Draw a landmark (for example a spline, key 3) and a selection, then build a GeoDataFrame from the widget (needs `geopandas`):

```python
import milume
from milume import landmarks_to_geodataframe
w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
gdf = landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
sel = w.get_obs_names(w.selections[-1]["id"])
```

`obs_key` names the `obs` column to group cells by; every output has a `group` column with its values. When `obsm["spatial"]` has x, y and z, the outputs also carry `z` and `z_bin` (1 µm bins by default, `z_bin_size=None` turns them off).

## distances

`distances(adata, landmarks, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None, z_bin_size=1.0)`

Per-cell distance to each landmark's geometry. A line or spline with a buffer only measures cells inside the buffer.

```python
from milume import distances
d = distances(adata, gdf, obs_key="cell_type")
d[["obs_name", "landmark_id", "group", "distance"]]
```

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-distances.dark.png" alt="Histogram of cell counts against distance to the landmark." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-distances.light.png" alt="Histogram of cell counts against distance to the landmark." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## composition

`composition(adata, landmarks, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None, z_bin_size=1.0)`

Counts and proportions of each group inside a shape or a line's buffer.

```python
from milume import composition
c = composition(adata, gdf, obs_key="cell_type")
c.groupby("group")["count"].sum()
```

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-composition.dark.png" alt="Horizontal bars of cell counts per group inside the landmark buffer." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-composition.light.png" alt="Horizontal bars of cell counts per group inside the landmark buffer." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## along_positions

`along_positions(adata, landmarks, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None, radius=None, z_bin_size=1.0)`

Projects cells onto a line or spline as a normalized arc position `s` from 0 (start) to 1 (end).

```python
from milume import along_positions
s = along_positions(adata, gdf, obs_key="cell_type")
s[["obs_name", "group", "s", "distance"]]
```

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-along_positions.dark.png" alt="Histogram of cell counts against position along the landmark, from 0 to 1." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-along_positions.light.png" alt="Histogram of cell counts against position along the landmark, from 0 to 1." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## enrichment

`enrichment(adata, obs_names, *, obs_key, background=None)`

Group composition of a cell subset (such as a selection) against a background, all cells by default.

```python
from milume import enrichment
e = enrichment(adata, sel, obs_key="cell_type")
e[["group", "count", "proportion", "background_proportion", "log2_enrichment"]]
```

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-enrichment.dark.png" alt="Horizontal bars of log2 enrichment per group; groups above zero are amber, below zero teal." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-enrichment.light.png" alt="Horizontal bars of log2 enrichment per group; groups above zero are amber, below zero teal." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## nearest_distances

`nearest_distances(adata, seeds, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None)`

Distance from every cell to its nearest seed cell, in XY and in XYZ. Needs x, y, z in `obsm["spatial"]`.

```python
from milume import nearest_distances
n = nearest_distances(adata, sel, obs_key="cell_type")
n[["obs_name", "group", "seed", "distance_xy", "distance_xyz"]]
```

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-nearest_distances.dark.png" alt="Histogram of cell counts against XY distance to the nearest selected cell." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/measure/plot-nearest_distances.light.png" alt="Histogram of cell counts against XY distance to the nearest selected cell." loading="lazy">
</figure>

## write_obs

`write_obs(adata, df, column, value_col, *, obs_name_col="obs_name")`

Writes a per-cell measurement back into `adata.obs`, aligned by `obs_name`. Cells missing from `df` stay NaN.

```python
from milume import write_obs
write_obs(adata, d, "dist_to_landmark", "distance")
adata.obs["dist_to_landmark"].describe()
```

The new column works like any other `obs` column, for example in `scanpy` plots or as input to the next `peek`.

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/api/peek.md

# peek()

Open LandmarksWidget on `AnnData` or `SpatialData`.

Full signature, parameters, and behaviour are documented in the [LandmarksWidget API](landmarks.md) (`peek()` section).

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/changelog.md

# Changelog

What changed in each milume release, newest first. Dates are the day the
release reached PyPI (Pacific time). Each section links to its GitHub release
for the full list of pull requests.

To check which version you have:

```python
import milume
milume.__version__
```

## Unreleased { #unreleased }

!!! note "Not on PyPI yet"
    Version **2.1.0** is on the release branch. `pip install milume` still gives
    **2.0.0** until the release is published.

Genes load on demand, the install is lighter, and docs follow a Diátaxis layout.
The public Python API matches 2.0.0. Internal widget traits changed as noted under
**Changed** and **Removed**.

**Added**

- Genes load on demand with an 8-gene picker (**Mean**, **Median**, or **Max** when
  four or more genes are active). See [Color & layers](ui/color-layers.md#genes).
- The [`use-milume`](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/blob/main/skills/use-milume/SKILL.md)
  skill installs with `npx skills add ckmah/milume --skill use-milume` or
  `python -m milume.skill install`.

**Fixed**

- The Inspect (**I**) shortcut works when the pointer is over the map.
- molab demos tell you to click **Run all**.
- Vertex-only lasso selections show Measure category counts.
- Escape in the gene picker only closes the popup.
- Python 3.14 installs no longer fail on an ancient `s3fs` build.

**Changed**

- `pip install milume` no longer installs matplotlib, polars, or leidenalg. Install
  them yourself when your notebooks or recipes need them.
- Dependency floors for spatialdata, pyarrow, and s3fs; a smaller sdist; a minified
  widget bundle; and a brighter default Inspect contrast limit.
- If your code read `w.gene_columns`, use `w.gene_names` instead.

**Removed**

- The `milume[demo]` extra. Use each demo's script header or `uv sync --group demo`.
- Internal traits `gene_format` and `gene_values` (not part of the public API).

**Docs**

- Recipes, tutorials, Datasets, and Concepts pages under the Diátaxis restructure.

## 2.0.0 (October 20, 2026) { #v2.0.0 }

Coloring and reading cells in a region each have one way to do them now, and
the Inspect cube draws cells as 3D meshes. This release breaks code written
for 1.3.x with no deprecation period, so read the breaking changes before you
upgrade.

**Breaking**

| 1.3.x | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|
| `w.set_color(adata.obs["cell_type"])` | `w.color = "cell_type"` |
| `w.set_color(gene_values, legend_title="APOB")` | `w.color = "APOB"` |
| `w.set_color(values)` with a computed array | `adata.obs["score"] = values`, then `w.color = "score"` |
| `w.set_points(x, y, color=..., color_map=..., ...)` | `w.set_points(x, y)`, then `w.color = key` |
| `w.color_by` | Removed. Read `w.color`. |
| `w.get_obs_names(adata, sel_id)` | `w.get_obs_names(sel_id)` |
| `w.get_obs_names()` for every cell | `adata.obs_names` |
| `w.get_focus_obs_names(adata)` | `w.get_obs_names("focus")` |
| `w.assign_obs_mask(adata, key, sel_id)` | `adata.obs[key] = adata.obs_names.isin(w.get_obs_names(sel_id))` |
| `milume.peek(sdata, labels="cells")` | `milume.peek(sdata, shapes="cell_boundaries_z")` |
| `w.volume["labels_url"]` | `w.volume["cells"]` |
| `w.volume_label_ids` | `w.volume_cell_rows` |

- An unknown color key raises `milume.ColorKeyError`. A gene that wasn't
  loaded, or a category column with more than 128 values, raises
  `milume.ColorValueError`. The widget stays as it was when either one raises.
- `w.get_obs_names(region)` returns a `pd.Index` instead of a NumPy array, and
  raises `KeyError` for an unknown selection id instead of returning nothing.
- A hidden selection still returns its cells. Hiding only changes the display.
- One Esc in Inspect closes the cube and leaves Inspect. It used to take two.
- Inspect needs a shapes element with per-slice cell polygons (`cell_id` and
  `Z_um` columns) to draw cells. Stores without one, such as Xenium and CosMx,
  open Inspect with the image only.

**New**

- Open, move, and close the Inspect cube from Python:

    ```python
    w.inspect_cx, w.inspect_cy = 120.0, 140.0  # optional, defaults to the volume center
    w.inspect_open = True
    w.inspect_cx = 150.0  # moves the cube
    w.inspect_open = False
    ```

    `w.inspect_open` also reads `True` or `False` when you open or close the
    cube in the browser.
- Inspect draws each cell as a 3D mesh built from the cell polygons. Meshes
  sit inside the image by depth, so image in front of a cell shows in front of
  it.
- Inspect has a minimap. Click or drag on it to move the cube.

[Full 2.0.0 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v2.0.0)

## 1.3.5 (October 14, 2026) { #v1.3.5 }

Lasso and Inspect polish. No API changes.

**Fixed**

- A quick lasso drag now makes a selection. It used to count as a click.

**Changed**

- Inspect always draws cell outlines, and the **Cut outline** toggle is gone.
  From the top, each cell shows as a ring you can see through.

[Full 1.3.5 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v1.3.5)

## 1.3.4 (October 11, 2026) { #v1.3.4 }

Lasso works on molab. No API changes.

**Fixed**

- On molab, lasso drags draw and make a selection, and page text no longer
  gets selected while you drag.
- Inspect cube framing, **Save** snapshots, and cut outlines on data with
  uneven voxel spacing.

[Full 1.3.4 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v1.3.4)

## 1.3.3 (October 11, 2026) { #v1.3.3 }

More molab fixes. No API changes.

**Fixed**

- On molab, selected cells are highlighted on the map and the Inspect cube is
  centered.
- Changing the cell or window size no longer resets the zoom.

[Full 1.3.3 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v1.3.3)

## 1.3.2 (October 10, 2026) { #v1.3.2 }

Lasso works in marimo, and default sizes follow your data's units. No API
changes.

**Fixed**

- Lasso selection works in marimo and on molab.
- The default raster bin and Inspect window sizes come from the µm-per-pixel
  units in your dataset's metadata. milume falls back to guessing from point
  spacing only when the metadata has no units.

**New**

- With a Z cut or crop, the cut face of the Inspect cube outlines each cell.

[Full 1.3.2 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v1.3.2)

## 1.3.1 (October 10, 2026) { #v1.3.1 }

Inspect works on remote kernels such as molab and JupyterHub.

**Fixed**

- Inspect images load on remote kernels. Panning in Inspect is also much
  faster on large stores.
- In marimo, the Inspect cube no longer fails with "Unexpected end of JSON
  input".
- A partial cut survives closing the cube, moving the map, and opening it
  again.
- A landmark's color in the panel matches its outline on the map.

**Changed**

- `pip install milume` always installs spatialdata. Platform readers such as
  `spatialdata-io` stay optional.

[Full 1.3.1 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v1.3.1)

## 1.3.0 (October 9, 2026) { #v1.3.0 }

Xenium and CosMx support, a docs site, and a much richer Inspect cube.

**New**

- Load Xenium and CosMx data through spatialdata-io. For CosMx, pass
  `spatial_key="global"`.
- A [docs site](../../index.md) with an API reference and
  [`llms.txt`](https://ckmah.github.io/milume/llms.txt) for coding agents.
- Inspect shows cells as points, colors by gene expression, and cuts cross
  sections. It picks contrast limits from the image and shows labels by
  default.
- Select several category groups within one selection set.
- Loading and error indicators on the map and in Inspect.

**Fixed**

- Moving the Inspect window no longer flashes, and toggling neighbors is much
  faster.

[Full 1.3.0 release](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/releases/tag/v1.3.0)

## 1.2.0 (October 4, 2026) { #v1.2.0 }

A reworked Inspect view, and smoother zoom on large sections.

**Changed**

- The Inspect cube opens when you release the mouse and fills the plot area.
- New selections are named after their top category and cell count, such as
  `Epithelial · 214`, instead of `selection 1`. Code that typed an old id
  literally needs the new name. Read ids from `w.selections`.
- Labels draw as outlined shells instead of filled cells. Default label
  opacity is 0.6.

**New**

- Shift+drag, or the **Move** tool, pans the Inspect window. Python sees the
  new position in `w.inspect_cx` and `w.inspect_cy`.
- Choose Additive or MIP projection separately for the image and the labels.
- Windows you keep with **Save** appear in the Selections list with a
  thumbnail. Hover any selection row to see its cell count, bounds, and top
  categories.

**Fixed**

- Zoom no longer stalls at the start of a gesture on large sections. Hovering
  a cell no longer shows a tooltip.
- Collapsed side panels no longer block page scrolling.

[Changes since 1.1.0](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0)

## 1.1.0 (September 30, 2026) { #v1.1.0 }

The first release under the name milume, formerly spatial-rx. The 3D cube now
lives inside the Landmarks widget as the Inspect tool.

**Breaking**

| spatial-rx 1.0.x | milume 1.1.0 |
|---|---|
| `pip install spatial-rx` | `pip install milume` |
| `import spatial_rx` | `import milume` |
| `VolumeCubeWidget(...)` | `milume.peek(sdata)`, then the Inspect tool |
| `GalleryWidget` | Removed |

**New**

- `milume.peek(data)` opens a `LandmarksWidget` for an `AnnData` or
  `SpatialData` object.
- `LandmarksWidget(sdata)` finds the table, labels, and 3D image in your
  SpatialData and opens them in the Inspect cube.
- Inspect shows a live preview under the cursor and loads the docked cube at
  full resolution. It uses about a third of the memory it did before.
- **Save** in the cube's title bar keeps the current window as an inspect
  selection.
- `milume.enrichment` and `milume.nearest_distances` join the measure
  functions. With 3D coordinates, `distances`, `along_positions`, and
  `composition` also report depth, binned by `z_bin_size` (1 µm by default).

[Changes since spatial-rx 1.0.1](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/compare/v1.0.1...v1.1.0)

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/datasets.md

# Datasets

Demo and test datasets by size tier ([#343](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/343)). Constructor and loader options live on the [LandmarksWidget API](api/landmarks.md#constructor-parameters); streaming colon is tracked in [#134](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/134).

| Tier | Dataset | Size | Cells × genes | Modality | Used by | Source / license |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tiny | `tests/data` fixtures + HF [`Stellaromics/demo`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Stellaromics/demo) `xsmall/` | Xenium ovary subsample 1,487,071 B; CosMx synthetic 6,311 B; `xsmall/` 8,277,419 B | 187 × 241 (Pyxa cube) | 2D Xenium outs; synthetic CosMx flat files; 100 µm Pyxa crop | CI, unit/e2e, docs tool stills | 10x example [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); synthetic (repo); Pyxa demo [BSD-3-Clause](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Stellaromics/demo) |
| 2D | `ileum_merfish_xu2026` | 5,014,135 B | 30,332 × 1,815 | 2D MERFISH mouse ileum (one SPF section) | 2D tutorials, recipes, how-to examples | Xu et al. 2026 / Dryad [CC0-1.0](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.p5hqbzm0z); [API](api/datasets.md) |
| 3D | HF `Stellaromics/demo` `small/` | 246,930,525 B (no transcript CSV) | 4,372 × 241 | 3D DAPI mosaic + per-z cell outlines (~1310 × 443 × 130 µm) | [Landmarks molab demo](https://molab.marimo.io/github/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/landmarks.py), 3D tutorial, Inspect docs | Stellaromics Pyxa demo [BSD-3-Clause](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Stellaromics/demo); left untrimmed on purpose |
| full | HF `Stellaromics/demo` `colon/` | ~30.2 GB | 492,155 × 1,020 | Human colon region + 3D mosaic | Showcase, perf, streaming work | Glasgow colon run + Stellaromics; [BSD-3-Clause](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Stellaromics/demo); see HF README [Colon attribution](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Stellaromics/demo#colon-attribution) |

## tiny

**Fields:** Sub-megabyte committed fixtures under `tests/data/` (`xenium_ovary_subsample/`, `cosmx_synthetic_tiny/`) plus the Hugging Face `xsmall/` tree (100 µm cube cropped from `small/`; 187 cells kept whole with segmentation and counts).

**Load:** Test helpers and frontend harness scripts read the committed paths or `snapshot_download(..., allow_patterns="xsmall/*")` then `spatialdata_io.experimental.pyxa`. Coordinates are in micrometres (Pyxa metadata; Xenium as read by `spatialdata_io`).

**Citation:** Xenium ovary tiny — 10x Genomics public example data, CC BY 4.0. Pyxa `xsmall/` — Stellaromics demo dataset, BSD-3-Clause (see HF README).

## 2D

**Fields:** AnnData with authors' log-normalized `X` (float32 CSR), `layers['raw_counts']` (int32 CSR), `obsm["spatial"]` (µm), `obs` columns `cell_type`, `cell_class`, `anatomical_layer`, `mucosal_pseudospace`, and `uns["cell_type_colors"]`. **1,815** QC-pass genes for the slice (nnz 920,437; median 26 genes/cell and 48 raw counts/cell over those genes). Source `obs['n_counts']` median 54 refers to the full panel, not this gene subset.

**Load:** ``import milume as ml`` then ``ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()`` or ``ml.datasets.ileum_merfish_xu2026()`` (``ml.ds`` is the same module as ``ml.datasets``). Downloads go to the user cache when the in-repo file is absent. From a checkout you can pass ``path="demos/data/ileum.h5ad"``. Registry metadata matches ``ml.datasets.info("ileum_merfish_xu2026")`` ([Datasets API](api/datasets.md)). Then ``milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type", genes=[...])`` with a short preload list in notebooks so exports stay under the static payload budget; omit ``genes`` or pass ``genes=None`` to rely on on-demand loading for all 1,815 names. Do not re-normalize: ``X`` is already log-normalized.

**Citation:**

- Xu RJ, Zhang H, Cadinu P, Nicol PB, Herrmann US, Lee T, Geistlinger L, Irizarry RA, Moffitt JR. *Cell Host & Microbe* 34(3):509–525.e13 (2026). [doi:10.1016/j.chom.2026.01.018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chom.2026.01.018)
- Moffitt J, Xu R. Dryad (2025), version 5. [doi:10.5061/dryad.p5hqbzm0z](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.p5hqbzm0z). CC0-1.0.

Provenance and regen: [`demos/data/README.md`](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/data/README.md), [`demos/data/xu2026/`](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/data/xu2026/README.md).

## 3D

**Fields:** Pyxa folder layout: `cell_by_gene_v1.csv`, `cell_metadata_v1.csv`, `segmentation_geometries_v1.parquet`, zipped `mosaic_3d.ome.zarr.zip` (optional transcript CSV). Table coordinates in µm; Inspect uses the mosaic and per-z cell outline meshes.

**Load:** `snapshot_download("Stellaromics/demo", allow_patterns="small/*", ignore_patterns="*cell_assigned_gene*")` then `pyxa(local_dir / "small", cell_assigned_gene=False)` as in [`demos/landmarks.py`](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/blob/main/demos/landmarks.py). Write a SpatialData Zarr store if you need a stable path for Inspect. Clustering in the demo uses `sc.pp.log1p` on counts only for a colour column — not `normalize_total`.

**Citation:** Stellaromics Pyxa demo dataset, BSD-3-Clause. Colon attribution on the HF README applies to `colon/`, not `small/`.

## full

**Fields:** Full human colon Pyxa export (`colon/` on HF): ~5180 × 4230 × 128 µm, 492,155 cells, 1,020 genes, ~30 GB on disk when materialized.

**Load:** Stream or selectively `snapshot_download` columns/files you need ([#134](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/134)). Not bundled in git.

**Citation:** Stellaromics Pyxa demo dataset, BSD-3-Clause; [Colon attribution](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Stellaromics/demo#colon-attribution) on the HF README.

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/keyboard-shortcuts.md

# Keyboard shortcuts

Global navigation and panel shortcuts. Tool-specific keys (lasso, landmarks, Inspect, Probe) are on each [Widget UI](ui/index.md) page.

| Action | Keys |
|---|---|
| Select | <kbd>V</kbd> |
| Move | <kbd>H</kbd> |
| Pan while held (any tool) | <kbd>Space</kbd> |
| Zoom in / out | <kbd>=</kbd> / <kbd>-</kbd> |
| Reset view | <kbd>0</kbd> |
| Full screen | <kbd>F</kbd> |
| Collapse left / right panel | <kbd>[</kbd> / <kbd>]</kbd> |
| Deselect, cancel a draft | <kbd>Esc</kbd> |

See [Navigate](ui/navigate.md) for toolbar icons that match these keys.

# https://ckmah.github.io/milume/docs/reference/ui/color-layers.md

# Color & layers

<figure class="ml-hero" markdown="0">
<video class="ml-loop" autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" data-src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/hero" data-theme="dark" poster="../../../assets/tools/color-layers/hero.dark.poster.webp" aria-label="The color panel switches from category to genes to embed, and the map recolors each time." width="960" height="600"><source src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/hero.dark.webm" type="video/webm"><source src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/hero.dark.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>
<img class="ml-loop-poster" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/hero.dark.poster.webp" alt="The color panel switches from category to genes to embed, and the map recolors each time." width="960" height="600" loading="lazy">
</figure>

Switch the color panel between category, genes and embed; the map recolors to match.
{: .ml-caption }

```python
import milume
w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type", genes=["GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneC"])
w.color  # obs column, gene, gene list, or obsm key (e.g. "X_pca")
```

## Color tabs

The right panel has three pill tabs. They have no icons, so the table names each tab.

<div class="ml-controls" markdown>

| | Tab | What it colors by |
|---|---|---|
| <span class="ml-badge">1</span> | category | An `obs` category column. Expand it (<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m9 18 6-6-6-6"></path></svg>) to toggle single subcategories. |
| <span class="ml-badge">2</span> | genes | Expression of the picked genes, with ridgeline densities and a blend legend. Pick genes in the field under the legend. |
| <span class="ml-badge">3</span> | embed | An embedding (for example `X_pca`) mapped to RGB, with an RGB-cube legend. Choose the embedding from the dropdown. |

</div>

### genes

Pick up to three genes to blend them, one colour channel each. Pick four to eight and
the cells colour by one combined value on a single ramp; choose **Mean**, **Median** or
**Max** of the picked genes' normalized expression under the gene field.

Each gene's values load from the kernel the first time you colour by it, so the widget
opens fast on whole-transcriptome panels (an 18k-gene Atera breast section included).
`genes=[...]` preloads a short list instead, which helps when the kernel is slow to reply.
A list that would pack over 64 MiB loads on demand too, with a warning.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/still-genes.dark.png" alt="The genes tab with three genes picked: ridgeline densities per gene, a blend legend, the gene chips, and Shared scale and log scale switches." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/still-genes.light.png" alt="The genes tab with three genes picked: ridgeline densities per gene, a blend legend, the gene chips, and Shared scale and log scale switches." loading="lazy">
</figure>

### embed

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/still-embed.dark.png" alt="The embed tab showing an RGB-cube legend and the embedding dropdown, with cells colored by their embedding." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/still-embed.light.png" alt="The embed tab showing an RGB-cube legend and the embedding dropdown, with cells colored by their embedding." loading="lazy">
</figure>

| | Control | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1"></circle><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10"></circle></svg> | points/raster | Flip between drawing each cell as a point and aggregating cells into raster bins (<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 3v18"></path><path d="M3 12h18"></path><rect x="3" y="3" width="18" height="18" rx="2"></rect></svg>). The icon shows the current mode. |

</div>

## Layers list

The left panel lists every selection and landmark.

<figure class="ml-hero ml-hero--still" markdown="0">
<img class="ml-only-dark" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/still-layers.dark.png" alt="The layers list with one selection row and one landmark row; amber callouts mark the two rows and their Layer actions buttons." loading="lazy">
<img class="ml-only-light" src="../../assets/tools/color-layers/still-layers.light.png" alt="The layers list with one selection row and one landmark row; amber callouts mark the two rows and their Layer actions buttons." loading="lazy">
</figure>

<div class="ml-controls" markdown>

| | Control | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| <span class="ml-badge">1</span> | Selections | Click a row to make that selection active. |
| <span class="ml-badge">2</span> | Landmarks | Click a row to select the landmark and open its context toolbar. |
| <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1"></circle><circle cx="19" cy="12" r="1"></circle><circle cx="5" cy="12" r="1"></circle></svg> | Layer actions | <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10.733 5.076a10.744 10.744 0 0 1 11.205 6.575 1 1 0 0 1 0 .696 10.747 10.747 0 0 1-1.444 2.49"></path><path d="M14.084 14.158a3 3 0 0 1-4.242-4.242"></path><path d="M17.479 17.499a10.75 10.75 0 0 1-15.417-5.151 1 1 0 0 1 0-.696 10.75 10.75 0 0 1 4.446-5.143"></path><path d="m2 2 20 20"></path></svg> Hide / Show, <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21.174 6.812a1 1 0 0 0-3.986-3.987L3.842 16.174a2 2 0 0 0-.5.83l-1.321 4.352a.5.5 0 0 0 .623.622l4.353-1.32a2 2 0 0 0 .83-.497z"></path><path d="m15 5 4 4"></path></svg> Rename, <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M10 11v6"></path><path d="M14 11v6"></path><path d="M19 6v14a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H7a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V6"></path><path d="M3 6h18"></path><path d="M8 6V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h4a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v2"></path></svg> Delete. |
| <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="18" height="18" x="3" y="3" rx="2"></rect><path d="M9 3v18"></path><path d="m16 15-3-3 3-3"></path></svg> | Collapse left panel ([) | Hide the list; see [Navigate](navigate.md). |

</div>

See [Methods](../api/landmarks.md#methods) for `set_color`, `set_raster_basis` and the rest.

# Inspect in 3D

<figure class="ml-hero" markdown="0">
<video class="ml-loop" autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" data-src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/hero" data-theme="dark" data-only-theme="dark" poster="../../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/hero.dark.poster.webp" aria-label="A 3D cube of the tissue volume, with the image and cell labels layered on, swings about 112° and back as the pointer drags the camera." width="960" height="600"><source src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/hero.dark.webm" type="video/webm"><source src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/hero.dark.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>
<img class="ml-loop-poster" src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/hero.dark.poster.webp" alt="A 3D cube of the tissue volume, with the image and cell labels layered on, swings about 112° and back as the pointer drags the camera." width="960" height="600" loading="lazy">
</figure>

Place a cube window on the map, then orbit and slice image, labels and transcripts together.
{: .ml-caption }

```python
import milume
w = milume.peek(sdata, image="mosaic", shapes="cell_boundaries_z")  # press I, then click the tissue
w.volume_cut  # cut-plane state after you slide the cross-section
```

## Entering Inspect

Press <kbd>I</kbd> or click <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21 8a2 2 0 0 0-1-1.73l-7-4a2 2 0 0 0-2 0l-7 4A2 2 0 0 0 3 8v8a2 2 0 0 0 1 1.73l7 4a2 2 0 0 0 2 0l7-4A2 2 0 0 0 21 16Z"></path><path d="m3.3 7 8.7 5 8.7-5"></path><path d="M12 22V12"></path></svg> Inspect, then click the tissue to place a cube window. The top pill shows the window size, <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 7v6"></path><path d="M15 10H9"></path><path d="M17 3a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v15a1 1 0 0 1-1.496.868l-4.512-2.578a2 2 0 0 0-1.984 0l-4.512 2.578A1 1 0 0 1 5 20V5a2 2 0 0 1 2-2z"></path></svg> Save window and <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="ml-icon" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M18 6 6 18"></path><path d="m6 6 12 12"></path></svg> Exit Inspect (<kbd>Esc</kbd>).

## Cross-section

<figure class="ml-hero" markdown="0">
<video class="ml-loop" autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" data-src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/loop-cross-section" data-theme="dark" data-only-theme="dark" poster="../../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/loop-cross-section.dark.poster.webp" aria-label="The pointer drags the cut slider: a cross-section plane sweeps through the cube and back; cell outlines stay visible on the cut." width="960" height="600"><source src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/loop-cross-section.dark.webm" type="video/webm"><source src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/loop-cross-section.dark.mp4" type="video/mp4"></video>
<img class="ml-loop-poster" src="../../assets/tools/inspect-3d/loop-cross-section.dark.poster.webp" alt="The pointer drags the cut slider: a cross-section plane sweeps through the cube and back; cell outlines stay visible on the cut." width="960" height="600" loading="lazy">
</figure>

See [Synced traitlets](../api/landmarks.md#synced-traitlets) for Inspect fields, and [Constructor parameters](../api/landmarks.md#constructor-parameters) for `image=` / `shapes=` on `milume.peek`. With several 3D images, pass `image=` to pick one. Stores without per-slice cell polygons (e.g. Xenium / CosMx) open Inspect image-only, with no cells; 2D image plus polygon rendering is tracked in [#122](https://github.com/ckmah/milume/issues/122).

Cell meshes run in an inline Web Worker. Strict notebook Content-Security-Policies must allow `worker-src blob:` (the defaults in JupyterLab and VS Code already do).
